History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
48-year-old man with asthma presents with 3-day history of persistent watery diarrhoea, central abdominal pain, and one episode of vomiting, most consistent with an acute infectious gastroenteritis; advised oral rehydration, monitoring for fever/red-flag symptoms, home rest, and in-person GP review if worsening.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Watery diarrhoea for 3 days.  
• Timeline: Onset 3 days ago; frequency “every 10 minutes,” no clear improvement or worsening.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Central, peri-umbilical abdominal pain; mild relief after bowel motion; mild tenderness on self-palpation.  
  – One episode of nausea and vomiting this morning after eating fruit (no haematemesis—red colour likely strawberries).  
  – Feeling of incomplete evacuation; needs to remain near toilet.  
  – Mild sweating past 4 days; no documented fever.  
  – Denies blood in stool, chest pain.  
  – Baseline asthma symptoms only; no new dyspnoea.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Pain partially relieved by defecation; uncertain dietary trigger; denies obvious food poisoning but suspects possibility.  
• Hydration/nutrition: Likely under-hydrated; currently limiting food intake.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No rectal bleeding, no melena, no dysuria, no neurological symptoms.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – uses inhaler (brand unspecified). No recent exacerbations.  
• No other chronic conditions mentioned.  
• Allergies: NKDA.

Medications:
• Inhaler for asthma – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Social History:
• Employed (unable to attend work due to diarrhoea).  
• Foreigner living in UK (exact details not provided).  
• No smoking, alcohol, or recreational drug history documented.  
• Reports inadequate fluid intake.

Family History:
• Father died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago.

Physical Examination:
• No vitals provided.  
• Self-reported mild central abdominal tenderness; no other examination findings documented.

Investigations:
• None performed or reported.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute watery diarrhoea with abdominal pain – likely viral/bacterial gastroenteritis  
  • Encourage adequate oral rehydration (water, oral rehydration solutions).  
  • Advise light, bland diet as tolerated.  
  • Monitor for fever, worsening pain, bloody stool, persistent vomiting, or signs of dehydration; seek urgent care if any occur.  
  • Avoid empirical antibiotics at this stage (may worsen illness).  
  • Stay home from work until symptoms improve (infection control).

Issue 2: Risk perception re: family history of bowel cancer  
  • Current presentation not suggestive of colorectal malignancy; reassure patient.  
  • If gastrointestinal symptoms persist beyond acute illness or develop red-flag features (weight loss, rectal bleeding, change in bowel habit >6 weeks), arrange GP assessment and possible colonoscopy.

Issue 3: Asthma – stable  
  • Continue regular inhaler use.  
  • No evidence that inhaler is causing current gastrointestinal symptoms; educate patient.  
  • Seek medical review if any increase in respiratory symptoms.

General plan items:  
• Follow-up: Patient to self-monitor for 24–48 hours; book in-person GP review if no improvement or earlier if deteriorating.  
• Education: Importance of hydration, recognising red-flag symptoms, and food hygiene to prevent future gastroenteritis.

Quality checks (document_quality):
Missing/expected elements:  
• Objective vitals and physical examination not available.  
• Comprehensive medication list (dose/route/frequency) and past medical conditions other than asthma not discussed.  
• Smoking/alcohol history not elicited.  
Internal conflicts:  
• Date of birth stated as 1 Jan 1992 but patient later says age 48 (implies DOB ~1972) – conflict noted.  
Transcript quality: Good overall; occasional background noise and minor verbal overlaps but clinically adequate.
